items.title: Magnarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I’ve played with many big bands, you know, the Glenn Miller Band and Toshiko Akiyoshi and Lionel Hampton

ctx.x: Well there are times when you’re playing music — I mean I can just speak for myself — when I’m maybe not feeling as inspired. It might not be my fault. It could be totally my fault. It could be that I partied too hard that week and my brain is shut off. And that’s not really an excuse but there are times when you have to go into your bag of tricks and maybe say let me pull this out here and see where it takes me whether it’s some kind of a pentatonic thing that you’ve worked out, or maybe it’s a circle of fifths…

it’s playing in half steps. These are things that you have worked out. Now I don’t go to a gig and plan to do these things. I never do that. But I do get in situations where — I am in situations where, yeah, I need to go there. And then I did a lot of big band stuff. You know I’ve played with many big bands, you know, the Glenn Miller Band and Toshiko Akiyoshi and Lionel Hampton, and a lot of times in those bands you only have 16 bars, 24 bars, and you can’t really be in a situation where you say well I’ll take…

On your Web site I think it was a video lesson on a Web site and you said you have to have big ears and you have to be an ear player, so you’re trying to play things that you’re hearing. How do you get a student to hear those things?
